A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLR optimizer work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A.1–A.7. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the figures, tables, equations, and proofs.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation experiments, training curves, DCoT evaluations, component ablations, qualitative examples, and memory measurements in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 2–6 and the qualitative image/video examples in Appendices A.3–A.5.

M1.justification: The three-part RLR estimator in Equation 11, its optimization procedure in Section 5, and the DCoT prompting and sampling adaptation in Section 6.4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pick-a-Pic and HPD v2 image tasks, ChatGPT-generated video training prompts, VBench evaluation, and hand-generation scenario for DCoT.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: Table 2 retains Base, DDPO, and AlignProp; Table 3 retains VideoCrafter, Pika, Gen-2, T2V-Turbo, DOODL, DDPO, and VADER. The DCoT and memory comparisons also retain their original comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices A.1–A.2 retain the same models, unseen-prompt evaluation, reward metrics, VBench weighting, batch sizes, diffusion steps, and training settings. The five-prompt DCoT experiment and its sampling interval are unchanged.

E4.justification: The truncation-collapse analysis, sample-efficiency curves, DCoT hand case study, component ablations, and appendix memory analysis are identical. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 3–4 retain identical error-bar displays. There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6, training curves, and qualitative examples report identical results. For example, RLR's weighted VBench average remains 84.61 in Table 3, and its total memory cost remains 22.4 GB in Table 6.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 4.1–4.2, Theorems 5.1–5.2, and Appendix A.7 assumptions, derivations, and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about RLR's unbiasedness, variance, convergence, generation performance, and the DCoT contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning truncation bias and collapse, RL sample inefficiency, multiscale generation, and RLR's memory tradeoffs are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The implementation link, appendix prompts, LoRA configuration, optimizer settings, perturbation scales, and hardware disclosure are identical. Both versions specify eight NVIDIA V100 GPUs with 32 GB each.

R1.justification: FLOPS: Forward Learning with Optimal Sampling remains the same cited work with the same attributed role. Its reference changes from ICLR 2025 to arXiv:2410.05966 (2024), with corresponding citation-year updates; this is bibliographic metadata rather than a change in cited-work membership or research positioning.

P1.justification: Three Ren et al. citation years change from 2025 to 2024 in Sections 2 and 3.2, the FLOPS reference metadata changes, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened FLOPS reference causes a small spacing adjustment in the left bibliography column on page 10, and the first-page margin stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 changes citation metadata, the version stamp, and minor bibliography spacing while retaining the same methods, evidence, proofs, explanations, and reproducibility information. These edits establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
